title: owed-decisions.jsonl (.dabbler/runs/owed-decisions.jsonl)
description: One row per event in the life of a decision the framework cannot make for itself. Append-only and repository-scoped rather than session-scoped, because an unanswered question outlives the session that raised it -- folding by `id` and taking the last row gives the current state. The shape is the education-mode brief: the operator arrives cold, may be watching several projects, and must be able to decide without reading the code. A row that states the question without stating a recommendation and a default has pushed the context-rebuilding back onto the person it was written for.

id.description: Stable across the decision's whole life. The fold keys on it, so a re-raise of the same question is the same row rather than a second one.

event.description: What this row records. 'raised' carries the brief; 'answered' carries the operator's choice; 'superseded' retires a question the repository outgrew without anyone answering it.

sessionNumber.description: The session that recorded the row. Null when raised outside a session.

severity.description: How much the framework is prepared to do without the answer. 'blocking' belongs to the verification-reduction class alone and refuses the close; 'advisory' proceeds on the stated default with the wait recorded. Written on the raised row and carried forward by the fold, so every current record has one -- a decision always begins by being raised.

class.description: Which human-required class the question falls in, checked in the rubric's own precedence. 'verification-reduction' is first and absolute: it is the only class that refuses a close, because proceeding on a default would let the record claim something verification did not establish. The other three proceed on their default with the wait recorded, so no engine is ever held open.

question.description: One sentence, in the operator's language rather than the framework's.

file.description: Where the answer lands, repository-relative. Null when the answer is not a file edit. The framework writes it; the operator never does.

determined.description: What the framework established on its own before asking. Its purpose is to prove the question could not simply be computed -- a brief that asks for something derivable is a framework gap wearing a question's clothes.

options.description: Each choice with what follows from it, in plain language. Never fewer than two: a single option is a notification, not a decision.

recommendation.description: Which option the framework would take, by label. Withholding one to seem neutral pushes the work back onto the operator, which is the failure this format exists to prevent.

onNoAnswer.description: What happens if nobody answers. For every class but verification-reduction this is what actually happens, and saying so is what makes a non-blocking question honest rather than ignorable.

answer.description: The chosen option's label, on an 'answered' row.

answeredBy.description: Only an operator answers. The enum is the point: no model may record an answer to a question reserved for a person.
